source.title: Are there any 'object detectors' in the hidden layers of CNNs trained to identify objects or scenes?
source.authors: Ella M. Gale; Nicholas Martin; Ryan Blything; Anh Nguyen; Jeffrey S. Bowers

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: Measures unit selectivity in CNNs using signal-detection outcomes, a different method that bears on whether interpretations based on highly activating examples predict where units fire.
record.gate_note: The paper directly measures unit selectivity and reports outcomes relevant to V6. Results from prior studies are not recorded as rows. It does not test the Qwen3 audit, neuron shares across language models, the Inception cat-and-car example, architecture/tool explanations, or neuron-based attribution graphs.
record.test_reason: The study checks whether units labelled from their top-activating images (precision on the top 60, or Network Dissection) actually fire selectively across the whole image set. It uses signal-detection measures on AlexNet, GoogLeNet (InceptionV1) and VGG-16. This bears directly on V6 in vision CNNs; the labels are class names, not natural-language explanations.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also report that under 5% of conv5/fc6 units yield consistently interpretable AM images. They conclude that CNNs trained for image classification do not learn object detectors in hidden layers, and that signal-detection measures should replace precision, CCMAS and Network Dissection.
record.recipe_differences: This study uses signal-detection measures and tests image-category selectivity in CNN units; it does not use the language-model explanation-and-scoring procedure in the claim sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports markedly different selectivity estimates depending on the measure: precision and CCMAS can be high while recall and false-alarm measures indicate poor selectivity.

fits_no_version.finding: Human raters judged activation-maximization images consistently object-like for only 4.3% of conv5 and 3.1% of fc6 AlexNet units, versus 59.3% of fc8 output units (Table 1b).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The share of hidden units in an early vision CNN that one visualization tool renders interpretable is low (under 5%). This is a single-tool baseline relevant to V4's estimates, not a test of their rise.

fits_no_version.finding: CCMAS and precision disagree sharply: fc7.31 has CCMAS .94 but precision .11, and CCMAS for the top and second classes is similar (Appendix B–C).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unit selectivity estimates depend strongly on the chosen metric.

record.problems: The AlexNet analysis used only correctly classified ImageNet images and a random subset of units (233 conv5, 2738 fc6, and 2239 fc7 units). The other CNN analysis focused on selected bus units rather than a broad unit sample. Uncertainty is not reported for the principal AlexNet signal-detection results.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing on tested V6 were left out. The paper's AM human-interpretation results and other measure comparisons do not directly test whether an explanation derived from activating examples predicts where a unit fires.

untested.parts: Shares across language models, dense and MoE models, and scale.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron, pose, recursive generalization.
Whether interpretable share rises with better tools or architectures. Only one AM-based share for AlexNet is reported, with no comparison across tools.
Language-model neurons and natural-language explanations; an audit-wide share of neurons whose explanations fail.
Simulation-based automated scoring of explanations on new text.

missing.what: All Network Dissection bus units in Tables A3–A5 (7 VGG-16, 17 GoogLeNet-Places, 25 GoogLeNet-ImageNet) had precision below .6. This is the broader evidence behind R7–R9.
For fc6.1199, 72 Monarch images (5.8%) had activation 0, and butterfly images span the whole activation range.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. Explanations here are ImageNet class labels, and precision is approximated automatically from the classes of the top-60 images rather than by human raters. The evidence for V6 is about class-label explanations in 2012–2015-era CNNs. GoogLeNet is InceptionV1, but only bus units are examined, so V3 is untouched.

versions.untested_parts: Qwen3-32B audit shares and neuron-pole job counts.
Similar shares across language models, dense and mixture-of-experts models, or scale.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron, pose, and recursive generalization.
Whether architecture, regularization, and tools cause interpretability differences or produce the stated interpretability estimates.
Whether attribution graphs built from a model's own neurons explain behaviour without a replacement model.

Does not test language-model explanations or provide an audit-wide share of neurons whose explanations predict firing. Tests selectivity of CNN units using image-category examples and activation outcomes.
Automated explanation scoring on new text and the share of neurons attaining good scores.

rows.subject: AlexNet
rows.operation_detail: Measured recall at perfect precision across analyzed units; fc7.255 had the highest score in the model.
rows.note: The text also reports that this unit had precision .97 and CCMAS .9, despite its low recall.

rows.subject: AlexNet
rows.operation_detail: Measured false-alarm rate at the threshold giving maximum informedness for the highest-scoring unit.
rows.note: The unit's maximum informedness score was .91.
rows.check: No layer is given for unit 3290. The unit is picked by top maximum informedness, not by an explanation from activating examples, so it bears on V6 only indirectly. Note the paper's 'false alarm' here is the share of above-threshold items not in the class.

source_check.problem: Unit picked by max informedness, not from an explanation; bears on V6 only indirectly.

rows.subject: AlexNet
rows.operation_detail: Reported the minimum false-alarm rate at maximum informedness among units in the model.
rows.note: Aggregate result; the paper does not identify a unit for this minimum.

rows.subject: AlexNet
rows.operation_detail: Measured false alarms for a unit described as a Monarch butterfly detector at the maximum-informedness threshold.
rows.note: The unit's precision was .98, CCMAS was .92, and maximum informedness was .82.

rows.subject: AlexNet
rows.operation_detail: Measured false-alarm rate using the threshold for the 60 most active items.
rows.note: The stricter threshold reduced false alarms but missed most class items; see R6.
rows.check: At the top-60 threshold, false alarms are low (.02), so the example-based label fits the top examples. This is the premise of V6, not its failure; the failure shows in R6. Reader's 'partial' is wrong when the row is read alone.

source_check.problem: Low false alarms at top-60 are the premise of V6, so absent is acceptable; failure shows in R6.

rows.subject: AlexNet
rows.operation_detail: Measured the proportion of Monarch butterfly images above the threshold for the 60 most active items.
rows.note: Only 59 of 1241 Monarch butterfly images were above this threshold.
rows.check: Recall of .05 (59 of 1241) shows the 'Monarch detector' label fails to predict firing on most class images. This is the V6 effect in full, not partial.

rows.subject: GoogLeNet (ImageNet)

rows.note: The text says the three displayed units had precision below Zhou et al.'s .75 detector criterion; the figure gives this unit's precision as 0.0.
rows.check: Value is readable from the figure caption text: precision 0.0 (CCMAS 0.52). It should not be 'figure only'. The unit label comes from Network Dissection IoU, not from top-activating images alone.

relationships.display_finding: Units labelled from their top examples had high precision but recall of only .05–.08 and very high false-alarm rates, and Network Dissection bus units reached precision of only 0.0–0.53.

relation.reason: Its results bear directly on V6.

tranche.reason: A different method (signal-detection measures and jitterplots) that asks whether units labelled from their top examples are selective.

source_check.notes: At max informedness, the paper's 'false alarm' (>99%, min .96) means the share of above-threshold images outside the class (1 - precision at that threshold), not the standard FP rate. The bus-unit precision in Appendix D uses the top 100 of the first 100 images per ImageNet class. No row records Table 1b: under 5% of conv5/fc6 units gave consistently interpretable AM images.

statements.correction: AlexNet fc7.255: recall at perfect precision = .08 (highest in the model); top-60 precision = .97; CCMAS = .9 (Section 4.1).
statements.problem: 'recall .08 at precision .97' treats .97 as the operating point for .08, but those are two different measures. .08 is recall at perfect precision (1.0); .97 is the top-60 precision.
